summary: Deployed a small inventory web application on node1, served over TCP 8181 via a systemd-managed service confined by a dedicated, enforcing AppArmor profile ('inventory-app'), while AppArmor remained in enforce mode throughout (no profile was set to complain, and AppArmor was never disabled). Verified the service, port, data, and confinement all survive a full native reboot of node1.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: Ubuntu 24.04.3, AppArmor loaded with 24 profiles enforcing (no SELinux present; AppArmor is the system MAC)
Confirmed no pre-existing inventory application; ufw firewall inactive, so no non-MAC blocker for port 8181
Created /opt/inventory-app/app.py: a minimal threaded HTTP server exposing JSON inventory data on 0.0.0.0:8181
Created system user 'inventoryapp' (no shell, no home) to run the service unprivileged
Wrote /etc/systemd/system/inventory-app.service (NoNewPrivileges=true, AppArmorProfile=inventory-app), enabled and started it

Authored /etc/apparmor.d/inventory-app: a named profile scoped to the python3.12 interpreter, app files, and network inet/inet6 stream; loaded with apparmor_parser -r in enforce mode (never set to complain, never disabled)
Iterated the profile to eliminate AppArmor DENIED log entries (added directory read, host.conf, stub-resolv.conf rules), restarted the service, confirmed zero new denials
Verified via /proc/<pid>/attr/current that the running process is confined as 'inventory-app (enforce)' and aa-status lists it among enforce-mode profiles
Verified curl to http://$NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns the inventory JSON payload
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, service active/enabled state, listening socket on 8181, AppArmor enforce status, inventory data response
Triggered a native `reboot` on node1 backgrounded with a short sleep so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec access returned (saw connection timeout, then reset, then success)
Confirmed boot_id changed (242af11e-49fb-4e07-a001-8016b2349acb -> eadcac43-ed11-410b-88c4-4a471137219a) and uptime reset, proving a genuine restart

Post-reboot: confirmed inventory-app.service active+enabled, listening on 0.0.0.0:8181, serving correct inventory JSON, process confined under 'inventory-app (enforce)', 25 AppArmor profiles in enforce mode, zero AppArmor DENIED entries

evidence.requirement: Inventory application serves over TCP port 8181 on node1
evidence.summary: systemd service started; ss shows LISTEN on 0.0.0.0:8181; curl to $NODE_IP:8181/inventory returns inventory JSON

evidence.requirement: System's mandatory access control (AppArmor) stays in enforcing mode while the app is served
evidence.summary: Baseline aa-status shows AppArmor enforcing; dedicated inventory-app profile loaded via apparmor_parser -r (enforce); /proc/<pid>/attr/current shows the serving process is confined as 'inventory-app (enforce)', not unconfined or complain

evidence.requirement: No AppArmor denials from the deployed service (profile correctness, not a bypass)
evidence.summary: Initial denials (dir listing, resolv.conf reads) observed in dmesg were fixed in the profile; after restart, no new AppArmor DENIED entries appear while the service continues serving correctly

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol for node1
evidence.summary: Captured healthy baseline (boot_id 242af11e..., active/enabled service, listening port, enforce status, valid data); issued backgrounded native reboot with ack returned before disconnect; polled through connection timeout/reset until reachable; boot_id changed to eadcac43... with uptime reset proving genuine restart; post-reboot verified service active+enabled, port listening, correct inventory data, process confined under enforcing inventory-app profile, and no AppArmor denials
